card: Drops the obsolete POSIX startup workaround in SetupEnvironment that caught std::locale runtime errors and forced LC_ALL to C.UTF-8. The fallback was originally introduced to prevent boost::filesystem exceptions on invalid system locales, but Bitcoin Core now uses std::filesystem which does not rely on POSIX locale. The PR also fixes GUI functional tests to test translations using -lang=nl_NL rather than relying on uninstalled host locales, and adds release notes for external scripts.
changed_since_previous: Added release notes advising that external notify scripts relying on the implicit fallback must configure valid locales explicitly.
evidence: PR description: 'This was added to work around boost::filesystem throwing when the environments locale was invalid. Boost.Filesystem has been removed, and std::filesystem doesn\'t use the locale on POSIX (and bitcoind never calls setlocale).'
Commit message: 'Alternative to #36399, which extends the hack further.'
problem: A legacy startup workaround caught `std::locale("")` exceptions and forced `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` to prevent `boost::filesystem` crashes on invalid system locales. `boost::filesystem` has since been replaced by `std::filesystem`, which ignores POSIX locale, rendering the fallback unnecessary while causing compatibility friction on platforms like illumos (#36399). In addition, functional tests relying on `LC_ALL=nl_NL.UTF-8` skipped translation checks in CI or warned if the locale was missing.

risk.why: Child processes spawned by notify scripts or nodes in unusual POSIX locale environments might fail if they relied on Bitcoin Core setting LC_ALL=C.UTF-8.

summary: Removes the `SetupEnvironment()` locale fallback workaround that set `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` when encountering an invalid POSIX locale. In functional tests, updates GUI test nodes to test non-English translations via `-lang=nl_NL` instead of relying on host environment variables.
